title: Reese Witherspoon’s Hello Sunshine to be be sold to media company backed by Blackstone
summary: Reese Witherspoon's media company, Hello Sunshine, is being sold to a firm backed by Blackstone Group Inc. for approximately $900 million. This acquisition is part of a strategy to create an independent entertainment company for the streaming era, led by former Disney executives Kevin Mayer and Tom Staggs. Witherspoon will continue to operate Hello Sunshine and join the new company's board, aiming to further the mission of telling more women's stories.

title: Google’s upcoming plans for Israel: a server farm and fiber optics network
summary: Google is significantly expanding its operations in Israel following being awarded a government tender for cloud computing. This expansion includes establishing a server farm in the Sharon region and rolling out an ultra-high-speed fiber optics network, complementing its existing subsea cables. These investments aim to ensure maximum availability of Google's services, improve local internet infrastructure, and enhance Google's presence as a global telecommunications provider.

title: Apple ranks as world's most profitable company: Report
summary: Apple has been named the world's most profitable company for the 2020 fiscal year, according to the Fortune Global 500 list, with profits increasing 3.9% to $57.41 billion. This marks a shift from the previous two years where Saudi Aramco held the top spot. While Apple leads in profitability, Walmart remains the top company in terms of revenue on the global list.

title: Why all roads of industry lead to purposeful innovation and a platform economy
summary: The article discusses how the platform economy is transforming various industries, enabling faster innovation, increased collaboration, and better customer service. It highlights how companies adopting a platform mindset can overcome traditional business model inefficiencies and leverage interconnected tools, especially in sectors like AEC. The piece emphasizes the creation of value through compelling platform capabilities and the strategic decision of either building one's own platform or integrating with existing ones, citing examples like Tesla and Netflix.

title: ¿Cuáles son las empresas españolas con más ingresos en 2020?
summary: The article discusses the "Fortune Global 500" list for 2021, highlighting Spanish companies with the highest revenues in 2020. Banco Santander, Telefónica, and ACS lead among Spanish firms but have fallen in global rankings due to the pandemic's impact. Inditex and Naturgy Energy notably dropped off the list, while Walmart topped global rankings for the eighth consecutive year.

title: Amazon to add delivery fee for Prime members who shop at Whole Foods
summary: Amazon is introducing a $9.95 delivery fee for Prime members shopping at Whole Foods Markets in several U.S. cities, effective August 30. This move indicates challenges in grocery delivery economics, even for large retailers, and is described as a pilot program to cover operating costs rather than raising food prices. Grocery pickup will remain free for Prime members.

title: DirecTV breaks free from AT&T
summary: After a disastrous six-year ownership, AT&T has completed the spinoff of DirecTV, returning the satellite TV service to being a stand-alone company. AT&T acquired DirecTV for $49 billion but lost nearly 40% of its subscriber base, leading to high "churn" rates. The new DirecTV, with AT&T holding a 70% interest and private equity firm TPG owning 30%, aims to simplify its message and repair its reputation, focusing on content aggregation and distribution, though it plans to discontinue the NFL Sunday Ticket package after the 2022 season due to substantial losses.

title: Gannett Relaunches ‘USA Today’ Streaming Video Platforms
summary: Gannett is relaunching its USA Today streaming video platforms, including USA Today News and USA Today SportsWire, expanding their presence across more than a dozen FAST platforms like Xumo, Roku Channel, and Amazon Prime Video. This expansion has led to significant audience growth, reaching over 25 million monthly views, and a 200% increase in average view duration. Gannett is partnering with Amagi to facilitate this digital growth and enhance monetization opportunities for its premium sports and news content.

title: AT&T's DirecTV to become standalone video business
summary: AT&T Inc.'s satellite television provider, DirecTV, will become a standalone video business as part of a deal with buyout firm TPG Capital. The new entity will launch DirecTv Stream, a platform providing access to various streaming services. AT&T will retain a 70% ownership stake, while TPG Capital will own 30% of the new company, which was valued significantly lower than AT&T's initial purchase price.

title: Deal Of The Century: How Michael Dell Turned His Declining PC Business Into A $40 Billion Windfall
summary: Michael Dell orchestrated a massive comeback for his company, Dell Technologies, transforming it from a declining PC business into an IT infrastructure giant with a $40 billion windfall for investors and a personal net worth of $50 billion. Through strategic leveraged buyouts, including taking the company private in 2013 and acquiring EMC in 2016, Dell successfully pivoted towards data center infrastructure, cloud management services, and the "edge" market. His financial engineering acumen and willingness to take on debt, combined with a correct reading of technology industry trends, allowed him to reassemble his empire and spin off VMware, solidifying his position in enterprise technology.

title: Baxter extends Amazon Web Services collaboration to support new digital health, data management projects
summary: Baxter is expanding its long-term partnership with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to focus on new digital health tools, supply chain efficiency, and deeper insights from business operations. This collaboration aims to enhance its DoseEdge software, improve supply chain responsiveness through AWS analytics, and further develop remote patient management systems like its AWS-powered Sharesource platform. The move is part of Baxter's ongoing "digital transformation" and builds on its recent sales growth.

title: Pennsylvania Employers Must Pay for Time Spent in Security Screenings
summary: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled on July 21, 2021, that time employees spend waiting for and undergoing mandatory security screenings on an employer's premises is compensable "hours worked" under Pennsylvania law. This decision in In re Amazon.com, Inc. contrasts with the 2014 U.S. Supreme Court ruling in Integrity Staffing Solutions, Inc. v. Busk, which held such time is not compensable under the federal FLSA. Pennsylvania employers must now adjust their pay policies to comply, recognizing the state's stronger wage protections.

title: Amazon and Best Buy Introduce New Insignia F50 Series Fire TVs
summary: Amazon and Best Buy announced a new lineup of Best Buy Insignia F50 Series Fire TVs, marking an expansion of their three-year strategic collaboration. These new TVs feature enhanced 4K Ultra HD resolution with quantum dot technology, Dolby Vision HDR, DTS Virtual-X sound, and integrated Alexa voice controls for an immersive entertainment experience. The companies also highlighted the success of their in-store pick-up option for Fire TVs, allowing customers to order on Amazon.com and pick up at Best Buy stores.

title: How to Use Snowflake to Connect Your Systems and Centralize Your Data to Prevent Customer Churn
summary: This article explains how to use Snowflake as a data hub to centralize data from various systems, such as AS400 and Salesforce, to prevent customer churn. It details the steps for connecting AWS S3 data to Snowflake using Snowpipes and integrating Salesforce data, demonstrating how a Senior Data Architect would implement this solution. The integration aims to provide a holistic view of customer information, enabling proactive measures against churn.

title: Baxter Begins Collaboration with Amazon Web Services
summary: Baxter International Inc. is accelerating its digital transformation by collaborating with Amazon Web Services (AWS) across digital health solutions, customer experience, and technology modernization. This multi-year strategic agreement focuses on leveraging cloud technology to personalize patient care, enhance customer experiences, and modernize business processes, building on their existing work of migrating Baxter's data centers to the cloud. The transformation has already enabled advancements in home dialysis patient management with Sharesource and pharmacy workflow with DoseEdge, while also improving supply chain resilience during the pandemic.

title: The world’s richest company is not a tech firm says Fortune list
summary: Fortune's annual Global 500 list for fiscal year 2020 revealed that Walmart is the world's richest company by revenue, not a tech firm, despite significant tech industry profits during the pandemic. China continues to dominate the list with 143 firms, while the US follows with 122. Brookfield Asset Management was the top Canadian firm, with Apple being the most profitable company overall.

title: FedEx plans to hire 3,000 in Memphis, 80,000 nationwide
summary: FedEx Corp. plans to hire 80,000 people nationwide, including 3,000 in Memphis, due to increased demand for residential delivery services driven by the e-commerce boom. The hiring initiative aims to address the rising need for its services across its various subsidiaries. This massive recruitment effort reflects the ongoing impact of e-commerce on the delivery industry.

title: Coronavirus: Starbucks, McDonald’s, Home Depot to require workers wear masks inside all locations
summary: Starbucks, McDonald’s, and Home Depot are reinstating indoor mask mandates for their employees due to the surge in COVID-19 infections caused by the delta variant. McDonald's and Target will specifically enforce these measures in high-risk transmission areas as identified by the CDC. These policy changes align with the CDC's updated recommendations urging vaccinated individuals to resume wearing masks indoors in certain settings.

title: QQQ Versus QQQJ: Who’s Winning the Battle?
summary: This article compares the performance of the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) and the Invesco NASDAQ Next Gen 100 ETF (QQQJ). QQQ, which focuses on large-cap tech companies, has outperformed QQQJ, a mid-cap focused ETF, across various timeframes. Chad Morganlander of Washington Crossing Advisors favors QQQ due to its higher quality large-cap names and stronger balance sheets.

title: Amazon invested nearly $15M in Seattle biotech company Nautilus, filing shows
summary: Amazon has invested nearly $15 million in Nautilus Biotechnology, a Seattle-based biotech company co-founded in 2016 by Sujal Patel and Parag Mallick. This investment highlights Amazon's ongoing efforts to expand its presence in the healthcare sector. The disclosure comes from a recent filing.

title: ETF of the Week: Bitwise Crypto Industry Innovators ETF (BITQ)
summary: This article highlights the Bitwise Crypto Industry Innovators ETF (BITQ), which tracks companies generating most of their revenue from crypto business activities, as a top performer. The article discusses recent crypto market catalysts, including rumors of Amazon accepting crypto payments and statements from Elon Musk regarding Tesla's Bitcoin holdings and Jack Dorsey on Twitter's crypto integration. BITQ is presented as a way for investors to gain exposure to the crypto economy through "pure-play" companies like Coinbase, Silvergate Capital, and MicroStrategy, without directly owning cryptocurrencies.

title: #DEFCON: A Bad eBook Can Take Over Your Kindle (or Worse)
summary: A security researcher at Check Point Software Technologies demonstrated at DEF CON 29 how a malicious eBook could exploit Amazon Kindle devices, gaining root access and full control. The attack leverages two vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-30354 and CVE-2021-30355) that allow for remote code execution and local privilege escalation. This exploit could enable attackers to steal Amazon accounts, delete books, turn Kindles into bots, or brick the device, though Amazon has since fixed the reported issues.

title: Goldman knows the way to a banker's heart is a free meal
summary: Companies like Goldman Sachs, Havas SA, and Janus Henderson Group Plc are offering free meals and enhanced culinary experiences to entice employees back to the office as pandemic restrictions ease. They are using food perks to encourage regular attendance, manage work patterns, and reinvigorate office culture, hoping to fill expensive office spaces and foster collaboration. While some companies are investing heavily in food, others like Revolut, Microsoft, and Adobe are embracing more flexible or remote work models.

title: ServiceNow Acquires Database Performance Software Company Swarm64 -
summary: ServiceNow has acquired Swarm64, a Berlin-based database performance software company, to enhance its ability to scale digital workflows and handle growing data volumes for customers. Swarm64, founded in 2013 and previously venture-backed by Intel Capital and Xilinx, specializes in combining analytics and transactional database functionality. This acquisition aligns with ServiceNow's broader strategy of evolving its offerings beyond IT service management and expanding its partner ecosystem.

title: Apple’s TV Box Is Now Mostly Pointless. Will That Change?
summary: The article discusses how Apple's TV box, despite recent upgrades like a faster processor and new remote, has become mostly pointless in 2021. It questions whether the $199 price tag is justified given that content is now accessible on many devices, competing with cheaper alternatives like Amazon Fire and Google Chromecast. The author suggests that Apple needs to re-evaluate the device's purpose to remain relevant in the streaming market.

title: Quantum Computing Stocks Are Having a Moment
summary: This article explores the current state of quantum computing stocks, highlighting that while many large tech companies are "dabbling" in the field, pure-play quantum computing investments are still rare and often speculative. It reviews major players like IonQ, Microsoft, Amazon, Google, NVIDIA, Honeywell, and IBM, noting that many fundamental breakthroughs and commercially viable products are still years away. The author also warns against speculative investments, particularly those involving new SPACs and OTC stocks, and suggests that true quantum supremacy may not be publicly disclosed.

title: Websites To Get Hired For Remote Virtual Assistant Jobs
summary: This article lists several websites where individuals can find remote virtual assistant jobs, including Fiverr, Guru, Freelancer, UPWork, oDesk, and Amazon Mechanical Turk. It provides brief descriptions of how each platform works and encourages aspiring virtual assistants to build a strong online presence and portfolio to succeed in the competitive market. The author emphasizes professionalism, persistence, and continuous networking.

title: Sephora’s beauty makeover at Kohl’s begins
summary: Sephora is launching over 70 shop-in-shops within Kohl's stores this month, expanding its online presence and offering exclusive beauty brands like Fenty Beauty and Drunk Elephant. This initiative, announced in December, aims to replace Kohl's existing beauty departments, with plans for 200 shops by fall and 850 by 2023. This partnership follows Target's similar collaboration with Ulta Beauty, intensifying competition in the beauty retail sector.

title: GE Healthcare Brings Radiology Without Walls to Resource-Constrained Small Imaging Centers With AI-Enabled, Cloud Imaging Solution
summary: GE Healthcare has launched Edison True PACS, an AI-enabled, cloud-based Picture Archive and Communication System designed to help resource-constrained small imaging centers and community hospitals improve efficiency and diagnostic precision. This solution addresses challenges like radiologist shortages and IT resource limitations, offering remote reading capabilities and seamless integration of AI algorithms. It is available as a SaaS or on-premise offering with flexible subscription models to match varying organizational needs and budgets.

title: Reese Witherspoon's $900-million deal
summary: Reese Witherspoon recently sold a majority stake in her production company, Hello Sunshine, to a group backed by Blackstone, valuing the company at $900 million. This deal is part of a larger trend in Hollywood, driven by the streaming boom, where private equity firms are investing heavily in content creation and talent. The move allows creators like Witherspoon to maintain more control over their projects and maximize their value in a competitive market dominated by streaming giants.

title: Amazon reveals massive insurance partnership
summary: Marsh has partnered with Amazon to launch the Amazon Insurance Accelerator, a new digital insurance network designed to help small business sellers on Amazon secure affordable product liability coverage. This initiative comes as Amazon now requires third-party sellers to obtain product liability insurance after reaching $10,000 in sales in one month. The Accelerator provides US-based small business sellers with access to quotes and policies from several leading insurers, making it easier to meet Amazon's requirements and gain peace of mind.

title: Workday selects Google Cloud as a preferred cloud partner
summary: Workday Inc., a provider of financial and human capital management software, has chosen Google Cloud as a preferred cloud partner. This partnership will allow Workday customers in various industries to deploy Workday applications directly on Google's cloud infrastructure, giving them more deployment choices. The agreement follows recent reports of scalability issues for Workday's software with large customers like Amazon Web Services and the State of Maine.

title: Oracle targets data warehouse rivals with automated features for HeatWave MySQL service
summary: Oracle has enhanced its HeatWave MySQL service with new machine learning-based automation features, dubbed MySQL Autopilot, to improve performance and target rival analytical engines from Amazon, Google, and Snowflake. The company claims these features make queries significantly faster and more cost-effective. Additionally, Oracle introduced MySQL Scale-out Data Management and increased HeatWave cluster size, aiming to monetize its widely used MySQL engine through a managed service offering.

title: Sonos Move vs. Apple HomePod: Which should you buy?
summary: This article compares the Sonos Move and Apple HomePod, helping consumers decide which smart speaker best fits their needs. It highlights the Sonos Move's flexibility, portability, and compatibility with multiple voice assistants and music services, contrasted with the HomePod's high-quality sound and deep integration with the Apple ecosystem, particularly Apple Music and Siri. The comparison delves into features like weather resistance, battery life, and integration with smart home platforms, concluding that the choice depends on user preference for portability, voice assistant, and commitment to the Apple ecosystem.

title: Marsh Brokers New Amazon Insurance Network Offering Coverage to Online Sellers
summary: Marsh has partnered with Amazon to launch the Amazon Insurance Accelerator, a digital insurance network designed to help small businesses selling on Amazon secure product liability coverage. This initiative comes as Amazon stiffens its requirements for third-party sellers to obtain product liability insurance after reaching $10,000 in monthly sales. The platform connects sellers with a panel of insurers and digital distribution providers, offering competitive quotes and policies to fulfill Amazon's new mandate.

title: Online Shopping Just Got Cheesier: Cheez-It® Debuts First Ever Online Store With An Exclusive New Flavor Drop
summary: Cheez-It has launched its first-ever online store, CheezItHQ.com, offering exclusive products, merchandise, and limited-edition flavors. To celebrate, the brand is releasing a Cheez-It Extra Toasty Superfan 4-Pack featuring three new "Extra Toasty" variations. The new direct-to-consumer platform aims to connect with fans and bring food innovations to market faster.

title: Expedia Group pushes back its full return to the office to January 2022
summary: Expedia Group has announced a delay in its full return to office plans, now targeting January 2022 for a hybrid model due to evolving COVID-19 circumstances. This decision follows similar moves by other major tech companies like Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and Apple. The company's U.S. offices are open to vaccinated employees and visitors in the interim, with a global evaluation for similar approaches.

title: ICICI Bank has done well on asset quality and growth compared to peers: Bank of America
summary: Bank of America has re-iterated a 'buy' rating on ICICI Bank with a target price of Rs 820 per share, citing the bank's strong performance in asset quality and growth compared to its peers. Despite a challenging quarter for the banking sector, ICICI Bank showed healthy operating performance, good growth, and controlled slippages, with Bank of America upgrading its ROEs and earnings expectations. The fund house believes larger banks like ICICI are better positioned due to superior book mix and provisions, expecting better performance in the coming quarters.

title: Amazon to construct delivery station in Pinellas Park
summary: Amazon announced plans to build a new 40,000-square-foot delivery station in Pinellas Park, Florida, which will serve as a last-mile distribution point. This facility is part of Amazon's broader expansion in Florida, including a large fulfillment center in Tallahassee and five additional delivery stations set to open by the end of 2022, collectively creating 2,000 jobs in the state. Pinellas Park's Mayor Sandra Bradbury welcomed the new business, highlighting its potential for job creation in the area.

title: Albertsons Names Sharon McCollam New President and Chief Financial Officer
summary: Albertsons Companies announced the appointment of Sharon McCollam as its new President and Chief Financial Officer, effective September 7, 2021. McCollam, widely recognized for her role in Best Buy's Renew Blue transformation, will succeed Bob Dimond, who is retiring. She will oversee finance, corporate strategy, IT, supply chain, and property development, leveraging her expertise in retail operations and digital growth to advance Albertsons' omnichannel and transformation strategies.
source: Abasto, Food and Beverage Industry News

title: Antisemitism Watchdog Gives Corporate Giants Failing Grades in Handling of Antisemitism
summary: Stop Antisemitism released a report grading major U.S. corporations on their handling of antisemitism, giving "F" grades to Google, Unilever, and Cigna for various shortcomings. The report criticized Google for not firing an employee with a problematic past statement and omitting antisemitism from diversity standards, Unilever for Ben & Jerry's stance on "Occupied Palestinian Territory" and lack of Jewish representation in diversity policies, and Cigna for similar omissions. Only L'Oreal and American Eagle Outfitters received "A" grades for proactive measures against antisemitism and fostering Jewish employee groups, respectively, highlighting a general failure of corporations to protect Jewish employees and address rising antisemitism.

title: Gartner Magic Quadrant for CCaaS 2021
summary: Gartner has released its 2021 Magic Quadrant report for Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS), consolidating its previous regional reports into a single global analysis. The report categorizes CCaaS vendors into Leaders, Challengers, Visionaries, and Niche Players based on their adherence to core capabilities like channel-agnostic customer service journeys and intelligent self-service. Key leaders identified are Genesys, NICE CXone, and Talkdesk, while the report also details the strengths and focuses of other market players.

title: What's Changed: 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Cloud Infrastructure and Platform Services
summary: This article analyzes the 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Cloud Infrastructure and Platform Services (CIPS), highlighting key movements and strategies of the seven leading providers: Alibaba Cloud, Amazon Web Services, Google, IBM, Microsoft, Oracle, and Tencent Cloud. AWS maintains its dominant leadership, with Microsoft and Google also holding strong positions in the Leaders quadrant by focusing on operational databases, big data, and edge computing, respectively. The report details the evolving strategies of Visionary and Niche Players, including Alibaba's expansion beyond Asia, Oracle's commitment to its cloud infrastructure, IBM's restructuring to focus on hybrid/edge computing, and Tencent's investment in network capabilities for gaming.

title: Procter & Gamble set to dethrone Amazon as world’s biggest advertiser
summary: Procter & Gamble is projected to surpass Amazon as the world's largest advertiser. This report from Ad Age Datacenter indicates a significant shift in global advertising spending.

title: Sonos ARC Review: An Upgradeable and Flexible Soundbar with Captivating Sound
summary: The review introduces the Sonos ARC as a high-end, modular soundbar system that delivers an immersive audio experience. It highlights the ARC's upgradeable hardware, seamless setup (especially for Apple users), and captivating sound quality, particularly when paired with a Sonos Sub. While praising its performance and modularity, the review also notes minor drawbacks like a hidden sleep timer, lack of HDMI expansion, and absence of DTS support.

title: Where Will Competition in Big Tech Lead Investors?
summary: The article discusses the competitive landscape between big tech companies, specifically Amazon and Microsoft, in the cloud computing sector. This rivalry, exemplified by their legal battles over government contracts, creates trading opportunities for investors. The Direxion Daily Dow Jones Internet Bull 3X Shares (WEBL) is highlighted for those bullish on the sector, while the Direxion Daily Cloud Computing Bear 2X Shares (CLDL) is suggested for investors anticipating a downturn in cloud computing.

title: Anexinet To Acquire Cisco Partner Light Networks For ‘Full Stack’ Data Center Offering
summary: Anexinet is set to acquire Light Networks, a Cisco Premier partner, to bolster its data center services, particularly in unified communications and contact center as a service. This acquisition, backed by Mill Point Capital, is Anexinet's second in a year, aiming to expand its "full stack" data center offerings and geographic footprint, specifically focusing on the East Coast and potentially other cloud capabilities. The founders of Light Networks, headquartered in Atlanta, will continue to lead the business.

title: Amazon Web Services in a new partnership with Wyndham Hotels
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has announced a new global partnership with Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, the world's largest hotel franchising company. This collaboration aims to enhance digital guest services across Wyndham's 20 hotel brands by migrating core reservations, property management systems, and data processing to the AWS Cloud. The move is expected to improve operational efficiency, lower costs by 45%, and enable personalized guest experiences through technologies like machine learning and a new mobile application.

title: Kroger kicks off pickup partnership with Google
summary: Kroger has partnered with Google to integrate pickup service functionality into Google Maps for 96 stores across Ohio, Kentucky, and Indiana, with plans for further expansion. This allows shoppers to manage their orders, receive reminders, and notify stores of their arrival directly through the app. The initiative aims to enhance convenience, attract new shoppers, and capitalize on the surge in online grocery demand driven by the pandemic and the spread of the delta variant.

title: JanSport Sues Wholesaler Over Amazon-Listed Products
summary: JanSport has filed a lawsuit against Bravo Wholesale, alleging the wholesaler sold "liquidated, used and often defective" JanSport backpacks on Amazon.com, misrepresenting them as new. The lawsuit details consumer complaints about the quality of the products and claims Bravo Wholesale used JanSport's trademarks without permission. While Amazon is not named in the suit, the case highlights ongoing issues with trademark infringement on third-party marketplace platforms.

title: Oracle MySQL champion Nipun Agarwal explains the challenges of scaling up algorithms for data migrations
summary: Oracle's Nipun Agarwal discusses the challenges and enhancements of MySQL HeatWave, particularly its ability to scale algorithms for data migrations. Oracle has seen significant migrations to HeatWave from other cloud vendors, including AWS Aurora and Amazon RDS, driven by customer requests for more automation and greater scale in data analytics, leading to significant performance improvements and cost reductions. The company has also published benchmark data and scripts for competitors and customers to verify HeatWave's superior performance.

title: Board of Directors
summary: This article lists the members of the Joby Aviation Board of Directors, detailing their professional backgrounds and expertise. Each board member's biography highlights their relevant experience, particularly in technology, aviation, finance, and large-scale operations, which are valuable to Joby Aviation's mission. The board includes founders, seasoned executives from major tech and aviation companies, and finance professionals instrumental in the company's growth.

title: How Consumers Are Using Mass Arbitration to Fight Amazon, Intuit, and Other Corporate Giants
summary: Mass arbitration is emerging as a critical strategy for consumers to challenge large corporations like Amazon and Intuit. This approach involves consumers collectively filing thousands of individual arbitration claims, which can overwhelm companies with fees and pressure them into settlements, effectively turning traditional arbitration clauses against the corporations that implemented them. While not a complete solution, it has proven successful in several cases, prompting some companies to reconsider mandatory arbitration policies and highlighting the need for broader policy reforms to protect consumer rights.

title: Alibaba Company Profile
summary: This article provides a company profile of Alibaba, detailing its business model, various e-commerce platforms, and other digital services. It discusses the impact of recent regulatory measures and fines from the Chinese government on Alibaba's stock performance, noting a bearish trend despite continued revenue growth. The article also highlights investor interest in Alibaba's cloud computing division as a key growth area for the company.

title: Microsoft Partnership Puts the 'S' & 'G' Into the 'E' in ESG
summary: Microsoft has partnered with Volt Energy to bring carbon-neutral electricity to underserved communities, addressing both environmental and social justice issues within the ESG framework. This initiative, while small in scale regarding initial power purchase, is seen as a significant step in pushing the boundaries of corporate environmental and social leadership. The article also highlights the Putnam Sustainable Leaders ETF (PLDR), which invests in companies like Microsoft that demonstrate proactive leadership in ESG issues and includes Microsoft as a top holding.

title: Vita Coco parent enters new functional beverage segment with Pwr Lift protein water
summary: Vita Coco's parent company, All Market, has launched Pwr Lift, a new line of protein-infused waters, expanding its presence in the functional beverage market. The drinks, available in four flavors on Amazon, contain 10 grams of whey protein, B vitamins, and electrolytes, and are marketed as post-workout recovery beverages. This move comes as All Market prepares for a potential IPO, aiming to compete in a growing but competitive functional beverage sector.

title: Google infringed five Sonos patents
summary: A U.S. trade judge has ruled that Google infringed five patents belonging to Sonos, related to smart speakers and associated technology. This preliminary decision by the U.S. International Trade Commission could potentially lead to a ban on imports of Google's smart speakers and Pixel phones. Sonos expressed satisfaction with the ruling, which they see as validation of their claims of patent infringement by Google.

title: Equifax Brings Differentiated Data to AWS Data Exchange
summary: Equifax is expanding its cloud strategy by offering various differentiated data assets, including consumer credit, commercial marketing, and economic data, through AWS Data Exchange. This collaboration aims to provide business customers with easier and more secure access to critical insights for improved decision-making and revenue generation. The initiative builds on Equifax's $1.5 billion investment in its cloud infrastructure, ensuring rigorous data security and compliance.

title: Amazon’s Move Into Podcasts Was a Big Advertising Play All Along
summary: Amazon's recent acquisitions in the podcast space, including the distribution rights for "SmartLess," are primarily driven by an advertising strategy rather than just content distribution. The company is spending over $20 million annually for exclusive early access to popular podcasts, aiming to leverage the unique podcast advertising model where shows and networks sell their own ads. This move positions Amazon to compete with market leaders like Facebook and Google in the lucrative online advertising market, using podcast ad sales as a key entry point.

title: CIBC, Itaú Unibanco, National Australia Bank and NatWest Group launch Global Open Finance Challenge
summary: CIBC, Itaú Unibanco, National Australia Bank, and NatWest Group have launched the Global Open Finance Challenge, a virtual event to foster innovation in the global open finance ecosystem. Collaborating with Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Oolys, the challenge invites innovators to develop customer solutions, focusing on digital services, convenient banking access, and sustainability. The event aims to transform the financial industry by promoting secure data sharing and customized product offerings, with winning teams receiving incubation opportunities and exposure to banking executives.

title: Music distribution startup Distrokid hits unicorn status with Insight Partners funding
summary: Distrokid, an online music distribution startup, has achieved unicorn status after receiving new funding from Insight Partners, valuing the company at $1.3 billion. Founded in 2003, Distrokid allows musicians to upload unlimited music to various online stores and streaming services for a flat annual fee, while retaining 100% of their earnings. The company claims to distribute over a third of all new music globally.

title: Walmart Launches Logistical Revolution
summary: Walmart is partnering with Symbotic, a robotics company, to automate its regional distribution network in 25 of its 42 centers. This initiative aims to revolutionize product distribution, cut costs, and increase efficiency in its supply chain operations. The move is a strategic step to compete with Amazon in the soaring e-commerce market, involving significant upfront investment intended to pay off through reduced labor costs and faster fulfillment.

title: Procter & Gamble regains its title as top global advertiser
summary: Procter & Gamble has reclaimed its position as the world's top advertiser, surpassing Amazon, with a marketing expenditure of $11.5 billion in its last fiscal year. This resurgence highlights the CPG giant's strategy of maintaining ad spending even during difficult economic times, a move that brand consultants argue has consistently benefited the company. While Amazon has the capacity to increase its ad spending significantly, P&G's continued investment in marketing has proven effective in sustaining its brand presence and sales growth.

title: The Digital Pulse: Outbrain, GearBrain's Content Recommendation Engine of Choice
summary: GearBrain introduces "The Digital Pulse," a new monthly feature focusing on digital trends, with its inaugural column highlighting Outbrain Inc. (OB). The article explains why GearBrain chose Outbrain as its content recommendation engine, citing better quality recommendations, higher revenue generation, and minimal impact on user experience and site speed compared to competitors like Taboola (TBLA). GearBrain emphasizes that revenue from Outbrain helps cover editorial costs while ensuring a positive user experience.

title: Opinion: Bullish optimism boosting ‘unicorn’ stocks is more like delirium — and a harsh dose of reality is coming
summary: The article argues that the current bullish optimism surrounding "unicorn" stocks is akin to delirium, suggesting that a harsh dose of reality is imminent for these highly valued private companies. It draws a parallel to the early, uncertain stages of now-successful tech giants, highlighting that most "half-baked ideas" fail, and entrepreneurs often operate without hard evidence. The piece implies that the market is overvaluing these companies and that their current high valuations are unsustainable.

title: Wipro's former COO Bhanumurthy Ballapuram joins Google Cloud
summary: Bhanumurthy Ballapuram, former President and COO of Wipro Ltd., has joined Google Cloud as Vice President for the Japan and Asia Pacific region. This appointment is part of Google Cloud's strategy to intensify its competition with rivals Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services in the cloud-computing market, amidst its ongoing expansion and executive hiring. Ballapuram will work with regional leadership to further Google Cloud's enterprise momentum and customer success.

title: MicroSectors™ Launches FANG & Innovation ETNs, 'BULZ' & 'BERZ'
summary: REX Shares, LLC announced the launch of two new MicroSectors Exchange Traded Notes (ETNs), BULZ and BERZ, issued by the Bank of Montreal. These ETNs are linked to the Solactive FANG Innovation Index, which tracks major U.S.-listed tech and internet/media companies. The products aim to offer sophisticated investors leveraged and inverse leveraged exposure to prominent technology and innovation stocks.

title: Digital Learning Platforms Market to Eyewitness Massive Growth by 2026 | Canvas, Nearpod, Top Hat
summary: A new research study by HTF MI evaluates the Worldwide Digital Learning Platforms Market, forecasting massive growth by 2026. The report assesses market risks, highlights opportunities, and provides strategic decision-making support, covering key players like Canvas, Khan Academy, Nearpod, and Top Hat. It details market trends, growth drivers, technologies, and investment structures, segmenting the market by type (Web-based, On-Premises, Mobile) and application (Corporate, K-12, Higher Education) across various global regions.

title: Amazon Enters India Wealth Management with Investment in Smallcase Technologies
summary: Amazon has made its first investment in India's wealth management sector by participating in a $40 million funding round for fintech startup Smallcase Technologies Pvt. Smallcase, founded in 2015, offers weighted portfolios of stocks and ETFs and has seen its user base double to over 3 million amidst a retail investor boom in India. This investment marks Amazon's expansion into wealth management, following previous fintech investments in India in insurance and credit.

title: Amazon Hits Chinese Sellers With Crackdown on Fake Reviews
summary: Amazon has begun cracking down on Chinese sellers who use "pay-for-praise" schemes and other policy violations to manipulate product reviews. This shift in enforcement has led to the suspension of over 50,000 Chinese retail accounts, causing an estimated $15.4 billion in lost sales, as Amazon seeks to restore integrity to its marketplace. Previously, the company had been more lenient to encourage low-priced goods from Chinese merchants, despite rules against incentivized reviews.

title: GDS Q2 results: Company acquires data center campus in Beijing, developing in Macau
summary: GDS Holdings reported increased revenues and losses in Q2, with revenues up 38.9 percent to RMB1.86 billion ($288.7 million) and net loss at RMB298.5 million ($46.2 million). The Chinese data center company expanded significantly, bringing six new data centers online, starting construction on five more, and acquiring facilities in Beijing and Shenzhen. GDS is also extending its reach into Hong Kong and Macau, with a new 20MW data center planned for Macau and a 7,200 sqm facility in Hong Kong.

title: David Droga, CEO and Creative Chairman, Accenture Interactive
summary: Accenture has appointed David Droga, founder of Droga5, as the new CEO and creative chairman of Accenture Interactive, effective September 1, 2021. He replaces Brian Whipple, who is retiring after leading Accenture Interactive to significant growth, including $10.6 billion in revenue in fiscal year 2020. Droga will focus on driving creative excellence, customer experience, and business innovation, leveraging Accenture's capabilities to sustain business growth.

title: Is Clean Energy Fuels Stock A Buy After Declining 8% Last Week?
summary: Clean Energy Fuels (CLNE) saw its stock decline by 8% over the last week and 5% over the past month following mixed Q2 2021 earnings. Despite this, the company, which focuses on renewable natural gas (RNG) from animal waste, is considered a potential buy for long-term investors due to increasing urgency in climate change efforts, favorable regulations, and deals with major energy companies and Amazon. The company is actively investing in increasing its RNG supply and aims for 100% RNG sales at its stations within five years, positioning it well in the growing clean energy market.

title: Corsair HS80 RGB Wireless Review: Upper-middle Class
summary: The Corsair HS80 RGB Wireless headset offers impressive sound quality with Dolby Atmos, a clear microphone, and PS5 compatibility, making it a strong contender in the mid-range gaming headset market. Despite requiring two software applications and having limited size adjustments, its solid build and premium feel justify its price. The headset is ideal for PC and PS5 gamers seeking excellent audio performance and communication.

title: Rapid, Automated Firewall Deployment Comes to AWS
summary: Palo Alto Networks has extended its VM-Series Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW) Orchestration feature to Amazon Web Services (AWS), simplifying the deployment, management, scaling, and monitoring of virtual firewalls. This functionality, previously announced for Microsoft Azure, aims to save time and effort for enterprises securing their AWS environments. It automates operational tasks and configures necessary AWS resources, providing faster security deployment, reduced complexity, and enhanced scalability for network security teams.

title: For Long-Term Investors, a QQQ-to-QQQM Switch May Make Sense
summary: The article discusses how long-term investors might benefit from switching from the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) to the Invesco NASDAQ 100 ETF (QQQM) due to QQQM's lower expense ratio. While QQQM is newer and less liquid, its cost savings over time make it an attractive option for buy-and-hold investors seeking exposure to the Nasdaq-100 Index. The Nasdaq-100 Index has consistently outperformed other benchmarks, making both ETFs appealing for growth-oriented portfolios.

title: Big retailers book pricey private cargo ships in holiday scramble
summary: Major retailers like Walmart, Home Depot, and Ikea are chartering private cargo ships and buying their own containers to bypass supply chain disruptions ahead of the holiday season. These unprecedented and costly measures are being taken to ensure shelves remain stocked amid surging consumer demand and port congestion. This strategy gives larger retailers a competitive advantage over smaller businesses facing inventory shortages.

title: Big Tech Is in a Perilous Moment. The Stocks Are Unstoppable.
authors: ['Eric J. Savitz and Max A. Cherney']
summary: Despite significant regulatory scrutiny, major tech companies like Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, and Facebook have demonstrated unstoppable stock performance. During the April to June quarter, these five giants collectively generated $332 billion in revenue, a 36% increase year over year, with all reporting better-than-expected profits. Interestingly, most of their stocks sold off slightly after the positive earnings announcements.

title: Toys R Us shops are coming to hundreds of Macy's stores
summary: Toys R Us is set to open shops in hundreds of Macy's stores, marking a significant return for the toy retailer. This partnership aims to bring the "world's biggest toy store" experience back to consumers through Macy's retail footprint. The move follows previous efforts to revitalize the Toys R Us brand after its bankruptcy.

title: With Amazon MemoryDB, AWS takes aim at Redis in the cloud
summary: AWS has launched Amazon MemoryDB for Redis, a new managed Redis-compatible in-memory database service. This service aims to compete with existing offerings from Redis, Google, and Microsoft by providing high performance and low latency for Redis users within the AWS cloud. While Redis acknowledges the competition, it emphasizes its differentiated enterprise functionality and multi-cloud deployment options.

title: Cybersecurity Experts Worried by Chinese Firm’s Control of Smart Devices
summary: Cybersecurity experts are concerned about Chinese firm Tuya Inc.'s control over smart devices given China's law requiring companies to share data with the government. This raises significant privacy and security issues for consumer data collected through IoT devices in U.S. households and other sectors. Experts are urging U.S. lawmakers to implement regulations or bans on Tuya and other Chinese tech companies to mitigate these potential national security and privacy risks.

title: Amazon vs. Netflix: Which is a better growth stock to buy?
summary: This article analyzes Amazon (AMZN) and Netflix (NFLX) as growth stocks, comparing their financial performance and future prospects. While both companies show strong growth, the author suggests Amazon might be the better long-term investment due to its diversified business, sustainable growth, and strong competitive advantages in e-commerce and cloud computing. Netflix, despite its rapid earnings growth, has a higher price-to-earnings ratio and a more specialized business model.

title: Intel wins Defense Department contract for cutting-edge chip foundry services
summary: Intel has secured a contract with the U.S. Department of Defense to provide chip manufacturing services through its new Foundry Services division. This initiative, part of the RAMP-C program, aims to expand domestic semiconductor production for defense applications. Intel will collaborate with partners like Cadence Design Systems and Synopsys to develop and test semiconductors using its advanced Intel 18A manufacturing process, expected to be operational by early 2025.

title: STARTUP STAGE: StayTick is a membership-based hotel booking platform
summary: StayTick is a membership-based hotel booking platform that offers users savings of up to 25% on hotel bookings for an annual fee of €25. The company uses its proprietary technology to find and compare hotel rates, highlighting the savings for its members. StayTick aims to expand its market presence in Europe and potentially add other travel products, while relying on direct outreach and partnerships rather than competing with large OTAs on marketing spend.

title: Official Disney Castle Posted on Zillow For Only $157.99
summary: Hasbro has launched a unique marketing campaign for its new Disney Princess Ultimate Celebration Castle by listing it on Zillow as an official home. This initiative, part of Disney's Ultimate Princess Celebration and World Princess Week, allows "buyers" to browse an interactive listing complete with intricate details, room descriptions, and fictional previous visitors. The toy, standing four feet tall, is available for purchase on Amazon for $157.99, blending real estate fantasy with product promotion.

title: AWS, Azure, Google Cloud: Which Will Pay You the Most?
summary: A Stack Overflow Developer Survey reveals that among major cloud platforms, Amazon Web Services (AWS) specialists earn the highest median salaries, followed by Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud. The article highlights that professionals focusing on IBM or Oracle clouds might be at a disadvantage regarding pay, likely due to lower demand for these platforms. It emphasizes the importance of continuous learning and skill development in the evolving cloud computing landscape.

title: He built an $8.9 billion fortune. Then the controversies began.
summary: Bom Kim, founder of South Korean e-commerce giant Coupang, amassed an $8.9 billion fortune and was initially seen as a new kind of self-made billionaire. However, months after Coupang's blockbuster IPO, a series of controversies have emerged, causing some South Koreans to re-evaluate their perception of Kim and his company. The article highlights the shift from initial praise for his wealth generation to current scrutiny over business practices.

title: Better operational decision-making through machine learning
summary: TC Energy, a leader in the energy industry, is leveraging machine learning to enhance operational decision-making, particularly for its Gas Controllers. Through a collaboration with Amazon Web Services, they developed "Autonomous Pipeline," a system that analyzes vast data to provide real-time operational recommendations, mimicking experienced leadership. This innovation aims to improve safety, cost-efficiency, create market opportunities, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

title: Like the QQQ ETF? Don't Forget About 'QQQM'
summary: This article highlights the Invesco NASDAQ 100 ETF (QQQM) as an alternative to the popular Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) for long-term investors. While QQQ is favored by traders, QQQM offers a lower expense ratio and a more accessible share price, making it suitable for buy-and-hold strategies aiming to capitalize on the growth of Nasdaq's largest non-financial companies.

title: White House to tackle cyber challenges with Apple, IBM, insurance CEOs
summary: The White House is hosting a cybersecurity event bringing together top executives from major tech companies like Apple, IBM, Microsoft, and Google, alongside financial and energy sector leaders and the CEO of Travelers Companies Inc. The discussion will focus on ransomware, critical infrastructure, supply chain security, cybersecurity education, and data breach insurance, aiming to secure public commitments for improved IT security measures and workforce training. The event highlights the unique inclusion of the insurance industry, whose policies are seen as crucial for widespread improvements in cyber defense.

title: Urban Outfitters’ Nuuly Is Launching A Thrift Store App
summary: Urban Outfitters' parent company, URBN, is launching Nuuly Thrift, a new app for online resale. This platform will be a sister to their existing rental service, Nuuly, and will allow users to buy and sell apparel and accessories from various brands using "Nuuly Cash" credits. The move aims to capitalize on the rapidly growing online resale market, which is projected to be worth over $77 billion in five years.

title: South Korea set to curb Google, Apple commission dominance
summary: South Korea is poised to pass legislation, dubbed the "Anti-Google law," that would prevent Google and Apple from mandating their proprietary payment systems for in-app purchases, effectively stopping them from levying commissions. This move would make South Korea the first major economy to impose such restrictions on the tech giants, who currently charge up to 30% commission. The legislation has drawn criticism from Apple and industry groups representing U.S. tech companies, who argue it could risk users' privacy, reduce trust in app store purchases, and potentially violate trade commitments.

title: Global X S&P 500 Tail Risk ETF Holdings
summary: This article details the holdings of the Global X S&P 500 Tail Risk ETF (XTR), which was established on August 25, 2021, by Global X. The ETF, with $3.96 million in AUM and 504 holdings, focuses on large-cap equities and aims to protect against significant market downtrends by purchasing quarterly Index put options. The primary holdings include major tech companies like NVIDIA, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet.

title: SK Telecom gets into subscription business
summary: SK Telecom is launching a new subscription service called "T Universe" on August 31st, offering discounts and benefits at various brands including Amazon and 11st. The service, with two plans under 10,000 won, aims to capitalize on the growing subscription market and attract millennial and Gen Z consumers. SK Telecom anticipates initial losses but expects to expand its user base to 36 million and achieve 8 trillion won in gross merchandise volume by 2025.

title: Target's stock buybacks represent a bet it will be more valuable in the future
summary: Target's recent authorization of a $15 billion stock repurchase program is examined in the context of capital allocation. The article argues that while buybacks are often seen as short-term thinking, they can be a disciplined use of capital when other investment opportunities don't meet ROI criteria. This strategy reflects a long-term belief in the company's future value, as demonstrated by past buybacks at significantly lower prices.

title: Amazon Announces Two New Cybersecurity Initiatives Aimed To Protect Organizations and Individuals
summary: Amazon announced two new cybersecurity initiatives to protect organizations and individuals: making its Security Awareness training available to the public and offering free Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) devices to qualified AWS customers. The Security Awareness training aims to educate against cyberattacks like social engineering, while MFA devices provide a stronger security posture for sensitive information. These initiatives are designed to help combat increasing cybersecurity threats by enhancing education and providing stronger security tools.

title: Six network protocols that signal an incoming DDoS attack
summary: DDoS attacks, though sometimes overshadowed by ransomware, have seen a significant increase in volume and frequency. Security and network operations teams can detect impending DDoS attacks by monitoring specific network traffic types. The article outlines six common network protocols (UDP, CLDAP, DNS, TCP-SYN, Application Flooding, ICMP) often abused in DDoS attacks and offers insights into the warning signs to watch for, emphasizing the importance of network visibility, packet brokers, and packet capture systems for detection and mitigation.

title: Alphabet’s Wing Nears 100,000th Package Delivery
summary: Alphabet Inc.'s Wing subsidiary is close to delivering its 100,000th package, demonstrating rapid growth in the drone-delivery sector. The company is bullish on the long-term efficiency and profitability of drone delivery, with plans to expand operations in the U.S. and Finland. Wing anticipates that this automated delivery method will eventually be more cost-effective than traditional ground delivery.

title: Urban Outfitters to Exit China Market
summary: Urban Outfitters is closing its Tmall store and exiting the China market, citing a "global strategy adjustment" and following other international brands that have struggled there. The move highlights the intense competition from local players and online sellers, despite China's robust apparel market. This marks the brand's complete departure as it has no physical presence or other e-commerce channels in China.

title: Walmart Goes Up Against Amazon and Uber to Handle Your Last-Mile Deliveries
summary: Walmart has launched Walmart GoLocal, a last-mile delivery service leveraging its Spark platform to deliver goods from third-party merchants. This move positions Walmart in direct competition with major players like Amazon, Uber, and Instacart in the e-commerce delivery market. While it aims to create new revenue streams and utilize existing logistics efficiently, the service faces potential challenges including a nationwide shortage of delivery drivers.

title: Microsoft hires former Amazon cloud executive Charlie Bell
summary: Microsoft has hired Charlie Bell, a prominent former Amazon cloud executive, as a corporate vice president. Bell's move to Microsoft's Azure cloud business is seen as a strategic win, as Azure competes directly with Amazon Web Services (AWS), where Bell previously held a top leadership role for 15 years. His initial role at Microsoft is currently listed under the human resources department, which is considered unusual given his background.

title: SK Telecom Introduces New Subscription Service
summary: SK Telecom launched T Universe, a new subscription platform, aiming for 36 million subscribers and 8 trillion won in annual gross merchandise value by 2025. This service partners with major companies like Amazon, E-Mart, Starbucks, Google One, and Xbox Game Pass to offer a wide array of products and digital services. The company plans to leverage AI and a network of offline stores to provide personalized subscription offerings, anticipating significant growth in the global subscription market.

title: Walmart's media arm to offer brands a tool to help manage digital ads
summary: Walmart's advertising division, Walmart Connect, is launching a demand-side platform (DSP) to help brands more efficiently manage and purchase digital ad space. This new tool, developed in partnership with The Trade Desk, will leverage Walmart's extensive shopper data to improve ad targeting and measure sales impact both online and in-store. The platform aims to expand Walmart's advertising revenue, competing with Amazon and other retailers.

title: Global X NASDAQ 100 Tail Risk ETF Holdings
summary: This article details the holdings of the Global X NASDAQ 100 Tail Risk ETF (QTR), which was established on August 25, 2021, and focuses on large-cap equities. The ETF aims to mitigate "tail risk" by investing in NASDAQ 100 stocks and purchasing quarterly index put options. It lists the top holdings including NVIDIA, Apple, Microsoft, and Amazon, along with recent changes in its portfolio.

title: Jessica Alba Shares Her Back to School Must-Haves
summary: Jessica Alba, founder of The Honest Company, shared her back-to-school essentials for parents and students, focusing on clean and sustainable products. Her recommendations include Back to School Kits for classrooms with effective yet gentle cleaning supplies, reusable face masks, sanitizers, and wipes. Alba also highlighted self-care items like soaking salts and a calming bath set to help unwind during the stressful school year.

title: As It Faces More Scrutiny, Apple Will Reduce App Store Fees If Publishers Provide Apple News Content
summary: Apple announced a new News Partner Program that will reduce its App Store commission from 30% to 15% for news publishers who provide content to Apple News. This initiative comes as Apple faces increasing scrutiny and criticism regarding its App Store fees from developers, competitors, and regulators. To qualify, publishers must supply all their content in Apple's preferred format, provide metadata, and maintain an active presence in markets where Apple News is available.

title: Electric vehicle company Rivian has confidentially filed for an IPO
summary: Electric vehicle startup Rivian has confidentially filed paperwork with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to go public. The company, backed by investors like Ford and Amazon, has raised approximately $10.5 billion to date and was valued at $27.6 billion in January. Rivian plans to deliver its first R1T pickup truck in September.

title: Gap Inc. acquires 3D fitting room startup Drapr
summary: Gap Inc. has acquired Drapr, a 3D virtual try-on technology startup, to enhance the online fitting experience for its customers and drive its digital transformation. This acquisition follows similar moves by other retailers like Walmart and Snapchat to integrate fit tech. Gap hopes Drapr's technology will help solve fit issues, reduce returns for its brands, and complements other strategic initiatives like its investment in Obé fitness and Old Navy's Bodequality size-inclusive program.

title: Amazon acquisitions: What does Amazon own?
summary: This article details Amazon's extensive acquisition history, highlighting how the company expanded from an online bookstore to one of the world's most valuable companies by acquiring over 100 businesses across various sectors. It lists Amazon's largest acquisitions, such as Whole Foods and MGM, and also touches upon Jeff Bezos's other ventures outside of Amazon, like The Washington Post and Blue Origin. The article emphasizes Amazon's "need-to-win mentality" in driving its acquisition strategy.

title: World's Biggest Stock Indices | Index Fundamentals
summary: This article explains the key factors that influence the prices of major global stock indices, including the S&P 500, Dow Jones Industrial Average, FTSE 100, and DAX. It highlights how economic growth, dominant sectors, index weighting methodologies, and currency strength play significant roles in their performance. The piece offers a foundational understanding for traders looking to grasp index movements.

title: XPO to stop hauling inbound LTL traffic in Albany, NY
summary: XPO Logistics Inc. will cease accepting inbound LTL shipments destined for Amazon warehouses in Albany, N.Y., starting Monday. This decision, revealed through a memo from XPO’s national 3PL account executive, is seen as a reaction to Amazon-bound freight monopolizing XPO's trailer capacity and causing delays. The ban aims to clarify the extent of its impact on third-party logistics providers (3PLs) and potentially address diluted margins from such traffic.

title: Wyndham Hotels & Resorts Taps AWS to Upgrade Global Cloud Infrastructure
summary: Wyndham Hotels & Resorts has partnered with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to enhance its global cloud infrastructure and introduce new guest services across its 21 hotel brands. This collaboration is a key part of Wyndham's multi-year digital transformation, aiming to automate reservations, simplify operations for franchisees, and improve the guest experience in over 90 countries. The move will allow Wyndham to increase business performance, reinvest 45% of reduced data center costs, and achieve its goal of running 90% of its infrastructure in the cloud.

title: This Toy From The Mid 2000’s Is Now Worth Thousands
summary: The article discusses the resurgence in value of the discontinued miniature wargaming system, Heroscape, from the mid-2000s. Originally costing tens of dollars, master sets and waves are now selling for hundreds to thousands of dollars, even up to $4,500 for a complete set. The interlocking hexagonal tiles and mint-condition figures with cards are particularly valuable, with even damaged parts seeing significant price increases.

title: Kroger is delivering groceries around Florida now. What to know and should Publix worry?
summary: Kroger has launched an e-commerce grocery delivery service in Florida using an e-commerce hub in Groveland, covering a 90-mile radius. This marks Kroger's first e-commerce venture in Florida without brick-and-mortar stores, utilizing automated warehouses and Kroger-trained employees for delivery. The move is expected to introduce competition to the Florida grocery market, particularly for established retailers like Publix.

title: BORROWING TO UPGRADE: Healthcare development projects to be funded by loan from Spanish bank
summary: The Bahamian government plans to invest $100 million over the next 18 months to significantly upgrade the country's health infrastructure, addressing issues like limited bed space and insufficient equipment. This investment is being funded by a MIGA-guaranteed loan from Banco Santander SA of Spain, with $89 million specifically for modernizing the public health system in New Providence to respond to COVID-19 and build post-pandemic resilience. Additionally, negotiations are underway for an estimated $40 million MIGA-guaranteed loan from the same bank to construct a climate-resilient facility at Rand Memorial Hospital in Grand Bahama.

title: Arlo Offers Comprehensive Third-Party Compatibility With Amazon, Apple, Google, Samsung, And Others For Seamless Smart Home Security Experience
summary: Arlo Technologies announced enhanced compatibility for its smart home security systems with major platforms like Amazon Alexa, Apple HomeKit, Google Home Assistant, IFTTT, and Samsung SmartThings. These integrations provide users with seamless control over their Arlo devices through voice commands, notifications, and live video feeds on various smart home devices, reflecting Arlo's commitment to a robust and integrated security experience. The updates aim to offer peace of mind regardless of the user's preferred smart home ecosystem.

title: Amazon Web Services works with Adobe Experience Cloud as it reimagines B2B marketing
summary: This article details how Amazon Web Services (AWS) leveraged Adobe Experience Cloud to transform its B2B marketing strategy, particularly in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. It highlights AWS's successful pivot to virtual events, such as re:Invent, and how Adobe's analytics, personalization, and marketing automation tools enabled a seamless and personalized digital customer journey. The collaboration aims to further enhance personalization and optimize customer engagement in future hybrid events.

title: JD.com ramps up omnichannel approach as it looks beyond e-commerce
summary: JD.com is expanding its omnichannel fulfillment strategy by incorporating brick-and-mortar retailers and growing its warehouse footprint. This shift emphasizes supply chain services over pure e-commerce, with the company now identifying as a "supply chain-based technology and service provider." The goal is to leverage inventory from physical stores for faster deliveries and greater efficiency, aiming for long-term growth by enhancing logistics capabilities and customer experience.

title: 13 Undervalued Wide-Moat Companies With Exceptional Leadership
summary: This article identifies 13 undervalued wide-moat companies with exceptional leadership, as determined by Morningstar's Capital Allocation ratings. The companies listed earn an "Exemplary" capital allocation rating and are trading in the 4- and 5-star range. The article highlights Amazon, Compass Minerals, and Roche Holding ADR with detailed analyst commentary on their capital allocation strategies.
